idiom_name: Akka/Pekko typed actor mailbox or JVM BlockingQueue
implementation_notes: Scala has no channel in its standard library, so the channel is either a JVM queue used directly (java.util.concurrent.BlockingQueue, as in the Java notes) or an actor: an ActorRef is a single mailbox, and Akka's documentation states that an actor instance processes one message at a time, which is exactly the one-consumer contract with the actor system supplying the dispatch. Actor mailboxes are in-memory only, so durability requires a persistent queue or a broker client (Alpakka/Pekko Connectors, Kafka), and a bounded mailbox should be configured when producers can outrun the actor.
pitfalls: An unbounded actor mailbox converts overload into heap growth; bounded mailboxes need an explicit overflow strategy or the system blocks/drops.
Akka's default delivery is at-most-once: an actor restart drops the in-flight message, so retry must be a protocol concern.
An ask-pattern timeout does not mean the message was not processed - retrying non-idempotent work on timeout alone duplicates side effects.
